title: What is the difference between UNION and UNION ALL?
description: Duplicate removal vs raw concatenation, the sort-based cost of DISTINCT, EXCEPT/INTERSECT, and column-matching rules.

data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between UNION and UNION ALL?

`UNION` combines result sets **and removes duplicate rows** across the whole combined result; `UNION ALL` simply **concatenates** them, duplicates included. The deduplication makes UNION meaningfully slower on large sets — it requires a sort or hash of every row to identify duplicates. If you know the inputs can't overlap (different sources, partitioned periods, already-distinct keys), UNION ALL is the correct, faster default. Related operators: `EXCEPT` returns rows in the first set not in the second; `INTERSECT` returns rows present in both — both also deduplicate.

**Rules that apply to both:**
- Same number of columns in each SELECT
- Matching (or implicitly convertible) data types, compared by position — column names come from the first SELECT
- ORDER BY / TOP apply to the **final combined result**, not individual arms (wrap an arm in a subquery if you must order it)
- Parenthesized arms can carry their own TOP/WHERE; FOR XML/JSON restrictions apply per platform version

**Cost difference:**
- UNION ALL: plan = concatenate (Concatenation operator) — near-zero overhead
- UNION: concatenate + deduplicate (Stream Aggregate on sorted input, or Hash Match aggregate) — sorts/hashes everything; on millions of rows this dominates the query cost
- Both arms may also benefit from indexes separately — the dedup pass happens after

**EXCEPT / INTERSECT:**
- `A EXCEPT B` — anti-semi-join semantics: distinct rows in A that aren't in B (NULLs are considered equal for this comparison — unlike joins)
- `A INTERSECT B` — rows in both (distinct)
- Both deduplicate; both compare all columns positionally
- Typical uses: finding missing rows (referential checks between systems), config drift between environments, overlapping date ranges

**When UNION is genuinely required:**
- Merging overlapping feeds (same users from two systems) where duplicates are real and must collapse
- Otherwise prefer: UNION ALL + dedupe logic only where needed (GROUP BY on a key, EXISTS filter) — targeted dedup beats global dedup

data.title: Concatenate vs dedupe, and set-difference flavors
data.code:
-- UNION ALL: raw concatenation — the fast default
SELECT Id, Email FROM Users_Seattle
UNION ALL
SELECT Id, Email FROM Users_Portland;
-- If a user could appear in both tables, they appear twice here

-- UNION: same query, but duplicates removed across the WHOLE result
SELECT Id, Email FROM Users_Seattle
UNION
SELECT Id, Email FROM Users_Portland;
-- Requires sort/hash over every row -> noticeably slower on big sets

-- Period merge where dedup is provably unnecessary (disjoint months)
SELECT Id, Total, OrderDate FROM Orders_2026_01
UNION ALL
SELECT Id, Total, OrderDate FROM Orders_2026_02;
-- Ranges can't overlap -> UNION would waste work for zero benefit

-- EXCEPT: rows in prod config missing from staging (drift check)
SELECT SettingKey, Value FROM dbo.Config_Prod
EXCEPT
SELECT SettingKey, Value FROM dbo.Config_Staging;

-- INTERSECT: settings that exist in both with identical values
SELECT SettingKey, Value FROM dbo.Config_Prod
INTERSECT
SELECT SettingKey, Value FROM dbo.Config_Staging;

-- ❌ ORDER BY inside a UNION arm (invalid without TOP/OFFSET):
-- SELECT ... FROM A ORDER BY x
-- UNION ALL
-- SELECT ... FROM B
-- ✅ Wrap the arm:
-- SELECT * FROM (SELECT TOP 10 ... FROM A ORDER BY x) a
-- UNION ALL
-- SELECT * FROM B

-- Targeted dedup instead of global UNION:
-- SELECT UserId FROM (
--   SELECT UserId FROM Seattle
--   UNION ALL
--   SELECT UserId FROM Portland
-- ) u
-- GROUP BY UserId HAVING COUNT(*) > 1   -- find only the duplicates, cheaply

data.title: The one-word perf review
data.text: When reviewing SQL, a `UNION` where inputs are provably disjoint is a free optimization: swap to `UNION ALL` and remove a global sort/hash from the plan. Conversely, don't 'optimize' to UNION ALL when duplicates are possible — the bug shows up as mysterious double-counts weeks later.

Interviewers want to assess:
- UNION deduplicates; UNION ALL concatenates — and the performance consequence
- Column/type matching rules and the whole-result scoping of ORDER BY
- Knowledge of EXCEPT and INTERSECT as set-difference/intersection tools
- Judgment: when dedup is provably unnecessary vs when it's load-bearing

items: Defaulting to UNION where UNION ALL is provably correct — paying for an unnecessary sort
Switching to UNION ALL when inputs overlap — silent double counting in aggregates
Trying to ORDER BY an individual arm without TOP/OFFSET — invalid syntax
Assuming EXCEPT/INTERSECT keep duplicates — they don't
Comparing with NULLs via NOT IN/NOT EXISTS vs EXCEPT without knowing NULL semantics differ
What operators in the execution plan distinguish UNION from UNION ALL?
How do EXCEPT and NOT IN differ when NULLs are present?
Can INTERSECT be replaced by INNER JOIN? What changes with duplicates?
How would you merge monthly partition tables safely with UNION ALL?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: UNION removes duplicates (sort/hash cost); UNION ALL just concatenates
Column count and positional type compatibility required; ORDER BY applies to the whole result
Default to UNION ALL when inputs are provably disjoint
data.takeaway: UNION ALL is the engine-friendly default; earn your deduplication — use UNION only when duplicates are possible and unwanted.
